summary: Keep the replication worker's leave-state socket beside the daemon API socket so long durable state paths do not exceed Unix socket address limits.

compatibility.detail: The worker binds only RUNTIME/API_BASENAME.leave-state.sock, with its persistent .sock.lock reservation beside it: fractal.sock uses fractal.sock.leave-state.sock. Preserve the entire API basename so endpoints differing only in extension also stay distinct. RUNTIME is the configured daemon API socket's parent (normally XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, otherwise STATE/run). An equal API/worker path is refused with typed InvalidInput before removing or reserving the API socket. Daemon readers share the worker's path function and try that socket first. For one release only, not-found or connection-refused at the new socket falls back to STATE/fleet/leave-state.sock, with debug logging of the attempted path. Remove the legacy fallback after one release; HTTP failures, timeouts and other connection errors do not fall back.

downtime.detail: The daemon and replication worker are separate supervised processes, not a single process. Daemon-first rollout remains supported while the old worker serves the legacy socket; restarting the worker then moves its listener and reservation to the runtime directory. Restarting only the daemon does not move an old worker's listener. Worker-first rollout requires restarting the old daemon before fleet leave-state or pairing admission can use the new socket.

manual.detail: Restart the daemon before the replication worker when upgrading. Custom API socket paths must leave room for the appended .leave-state.sock suffix. Bind failures name the full socket path, byte length and platform limit (107 bytes on Linux, 103 on macOS).

recovery.detail: If a configured runtime path is too long, configure the daemon API socket in a shorter directory and restart both processes with the same configuration. Durable fleet state remains in STATE/fleet; no data migration or lock-file deletion is needed.
